human_alias: 第7次主训练尝试：任务保护执行教学版

budget.basis: same live executor tokenizer; full text and metadata, no programs

diagnoses.rule_anchor: Classify by the statutory category: firearms under Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10), each motor vehicle as a candidate under § 33-1125(8), wearing apparel under § 33-1125(1), and only engagement or wedding rings under § 33-1125(4). In EC, a value or aggregate ceiling limits protection rather than citation eligibility, and the one-vehicle language does not require final portfolio allocation among separately listed vehicle candidates.

budget.basis: same live executor tokenizer; full text and metadata, no programs

diagnoses.rule_anchor: Do not treat a pendant, bracelet, watch, or other adornment as wearing apparel, extend the ring exemption to jewelry that is not an engagement or wedding ring, or perform a final allocation between separately listed vehicle candidates.
For every owned asset, add a separate 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) output entry after evaluating specific exemptions.
The phrase “any other property” supplies an independent alternative even when apparel, motor-vehicle, or prescribed-health-aid protection also applies.
For every owned asset, emit 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 independently and report the lesser of whole-asset value and $300 for one debtor or $600 for two equal joint debtors.

by_task.when: Arizona exemptions are allowable and the asset is a firearm, motor vehicle, apparel item, or item of jewelry.
by_task.procedure: Classify before valuing: use Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10) for firearms up to $2,000, § 33-1125(8) for each separately listed motor-vehicle candidate up to $15,000, § 33-1125(1) for actual wearing apparel up to $500, and § 33-1125(4) only for engagement or wedding rings up to $2,000. For each eligible alternative, report the lesser of the whole asset's value and its stated ceiling.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not treat a pendant, bracelet, watch, or other adornment as wearing apparel or as household furniture, furnishings, goods, or appliances under § 33-1123; do not extend the ring exemption to jewelry that is not an engagement or wedding ring or perform final allocation between separately listed vehicle candidates.

EV_proposed_blocks.rationale: The parent correctly rejected non-ring jewelry under the personal-item paragraphs but then added § 33-1123 to a locket and necklace. The added boundary excludes jewelry from that household-property alternative without broadening Arizona categories.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and the debtor or debtors own an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: For each owned asset, first emit a separate 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) entry, then retain every independently matching specific alternative. Count debtors from the facts: use a $15,425 whole-asset ceiling for one debtor or $30,850 for two equal joint debtors, and report the lesser of whole-asset value and that ceiling. A simultaneous § 522(d)(1) entry does not reduce this independently evaluated ceiling. Before submitting, check every owned asset for its (d)(5) entry.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 522(d)(5) because a specific exemption applies, use $1,475, apply the one-debtor ceiling to two joint debtors, or return only a debtor's half-interest.

EV_proposed_blocks.rationale: Current joint-debtor outputs again used $1,475 or $15,425 and one response expanded into invalid output. The revised EV procedure makes debtor counting, whole-asset comparison, independent inclusion and final verification one ordered checklist while preserving EC verbatim.

by_task.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
by_task.procedure: Begin each qualifying asset's output with a separate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) entry, including vehicles, apparel, prescribed aids, firearms, jewelry, animals, musical instruments and household items. Report the lesser of whole-asset value and $4,000 for one debtor or $8,000 for two equal joint debtors. Then add every fact-supported specific subsection independently.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real or explicitly business-use property, omit it because another subsection applies, classify jewelry as necessary apparel, or infer § 12-1001(d) without explicit trade-use facts.

EV_proposed_blocks.rationale: Despite the existing independent-alternative sentence, the parent omitted § 12-1001(b) from a personally held firearm and a jointly owned vehicle. The ordered per-asset pass supplies concrete factual categories while retaining the real-property, business-use, apparel and trade-tool boundaries.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania exemptions are allowable and the debtor or debtors own an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: For each owned asset, first emit 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 and report the lesser of whole-asset value and $300 for one debtor or $600 for two equal joint debtors. Independently add § 8124(a)(1) only for actual wearing apparel, (a)(2) only for a Bible or school book, (a)(3) only for a qualifying sewing machine, and (a)(4) only for a service member's uniform or accoutrements. Those qualifying § 8124(a) entries have no stated dollar ceiling, so report the whole asset's value.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 8123 because another exemption applies or copy its ceiling into a § 8124(a) entry. Do not attach § 8124(a) to household textiles, appliances, vehicles, firearms, instruments, ordinary jewelry, animals or other property outside its stated classes.

EV_proposed_blocks.rationale: The parent repeatedly used one spouse's § 8123 ceiling, omitted § 8123, invented § 8124 classes, and copied $300 into a valid apparel entry. The revision separates the general-entry calculation from the closed particular-property classes and states their whole-asset valuation.
